newsitem.title: UK: Zaire frees British refugee-aid pilot after months.
newsitem.headline: Zaire frees British refugee-aid pilot after months.

text.p: A British refugee-supply pilot detained by Zaire since July was released on Wednesday, the Foreign Office said.
It said Captain Glen Neville-Smith had left the Zairean town of Goma and was flying to Entebbe in Uganda.
A spokesman said he did not know whether Smith's three crew, one of whom was Spanish, were with him.
"I would imagine as a good captain he would have insisted on his crew going with him, but I don't even know if he is on the same aircraft he arrived in," the spokesman said.
Britain used a visit to London by Zaire's Prime Minister Kengo wa Dondo on Tuesday to demand Neville-Smith's release.
Neville-Smith, who had been flying aid to a refugee camp in Goma, was held at a hotel after his plane was discovered to be carrying military berets along with the supplies.
The owners of the plane, Liberia World Airlines, have said the berets were intended for the Ugandan Army and were mistakenly put on board.
Tension has been rising in recent weeks in eastern Zaire, home to over a million Hutu refugees from Rwanda and Burundi.

The refugees have been in Zaire since Rwanda's 1994 civil war, but fighting has widened since the Zaire army got drawn into long-running ethnic clashes between Tutsi immigrants, known as Banyamulenge, and local Zaireans.
The United Nations has said it fears a new crisis in Zaire, which could parallel the Rwandan war.
